stem: Which of the following organometallic compounds strictly obeys the 18-electron rule?

verdicts.working: Each η⁵-C₅H₅⁻ ligand donates 6 electrons. Ferrocene has Fe²⁺ (d⁶), giving 6 + 2(6) = 18 electrons. The others have 19 (cobaltocene), 20 (nickelocene), and 16 (chromocene).

working:
All four are metallocenes of general formula M(η5-C5H5)2. The cyclopentadienyl ligand (C5H5⁻) is a 6-electron donor. The metals are in the +2 oxidation state with dn configuration: Fe(II) d6, Co(II) d7, Ni(II) d8, Cr(II) d4.
Total valence electron count = group electrons (dn) + 2×6.
A (ferrocene): 6 + 12 = 18e (strictly obeying the rule).
B (cobaltocene): 7 + 12 = 19e.
C (nickelocene): 8 + 12 = 20e.
D (chromocene): 4 + 12 = 16e.
Thus only ferrocene has an 18-electron configuration.

Independent check: Each η⁵-C₅H₅⁻ ligand donates 6 electrons. Ferrocene has Fe²⁺ (d⁶), giving 6 + 2(6) = 18 electrons. The others have 19 (cobaltocene), 20 (nickelocene), and 16 (chromocene).
solution:
Each $eta^5$-$C_5H_5^-$ ligand donates $6$ electrons; in ferrocene, $Fe^{2+}$ is $d^6$.
$$6+2(6)=18\text{ electrons}$$
Hence ferrocene obeys the 18-electron rule.
